A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NormXLogit work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original perturbation experiments on SST-2, MultiNLI, and STS-B, plus evidence-alignment experiments on BLiMP.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds QNLI evaluation, classification-accuracy results, and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: LogAt and NormXLogit retain the same classification and regression formulas, embedding-norm multiplication, and layer-wise application. Expanded explanations introduce no new algorithmic component or procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds QNLI question–sentence entailment evaluation using Llama 2, DeBERTa, and BERT. SST-2, MultiNLI, STS-B, and the same five BLiMP paradigms remain, making this a limited coverage extension.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged in the corresponding faithfulness and BLiMP experiments. Value Zeroing already appears in v1's BERT/SST-2 comparison. QNLI and efficiency experiments reuse previously evaluated methods; abbreviated baseline names do not indicate new methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds classification accuracy alongside AOPC and introduces distinct efficiency protocols: BERT timing at 40, 120, 360, and 512 tokens, and maximum feasible batch sizes under a 48GB memory constraint. Existing perturbation and BLiMP procedures remain.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Tables 4–5 add controlled analyses of runtime sensitivity to input length and batching capacity under fixed memory. These substantively test scalability previously discussed qualitatively. Existing component comparisons and the LogAt('plural') analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 4–5 newly report timing means and standard deviations over five runs. This reporting is confined to efficiency measurements and does not establish additional runs for retained attribution-quality results. V1's statement about setting seeds disappears with its checklist.

E6.justification: All retained Table 1 values and BLiMP heatmaps are unchanged. Substantial additions comprise QNLI scores, classification accuracies in Table 3, and timing/batch-capacity results in Tables 4–5. For example, QNLI AOPC for NormXLogit is newly reported as 0.363, 0.474, and 0.402 for Llama 2, DeBERTa, and BERT.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes explicit background formulas for sublayer normalization, head concatenation, residual updates, and the feed-forward network (v1 Equations 1 and 3–6). Attribution and evaluation-metric definitions remain unchanged. The new worked example illustrates existing metrics without adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the layer-wise performance claim from superiority to competitiveness. The introduction adds an explicit plausibility claim and qualifies architecture-agnostic generalization as applying across Transformer models. The central NormXLogit contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation linking strong embedding-norm performance on STS-B to sentence structure and informative rare words. It explicitly interprets BLiMP alignment as assessing plausibility as well as faithfulness, and adds limitations concerning evaluation gold standards, text/Transformer coverage, and token-wise representations.

D1.justification: V2 documents settings for the new efficiency experiments but removes the requirements.txt reference and checklist disclosures about supplementary code, seed locations, remaining hyperparameters, and future public release. Hardware, operating system, LoRA rank, and Integrated Gradients step counts are retained. Actual external code availability cannot be established from these PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds the GLUE reference supporting QNLI and removes references to Adebayo et al., the two Li et al. works, and SmoothGrad. Related work is condensed, including omission of DecompX's classification-head discussion, while the principal comparison families and positioning remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and Transformer background undergo substantial condensation and rewriting. Experimental motivations and layer-wise attribution explanations are reorganized, a Limitations section and worked metric example are added, and the reproducibility checklist is removed. The six main scientific sections retain their order.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the schematic and faithfulness plots as vector graphics, expands Table 1 with QNLI and second-best underlining, and adds Tables 3–5 plus classification-accuracy and QNLI plots. Layout and appendix placement change substantially. Regression plot axes are corrected from AOPC to Accuracy; BLiMP heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: QNLI and classification-accuracy results broaden empirical support, while Tables 4–5 provide repeated-run measurements for v1's qualitative efficiency claims. Clearer limitations and the worked metric example also help readers assess the work. These gains outweigh the limited loss of code and seed documentation references, but efficiency evidence remains confined to BERT and attribution-quality results still lack uncertainty estimates.
